newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique begins maize exports - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique begins maize exports - paper.

text.p: Mozambique, until recently heavily dependent on international food aid, has begun exporting maize, Maputo daily newspaper Mediafax reported on Thursday.
Some 13,500 tonnes of maize, believed to be destined for either Mexico or Malaysia, has been exported from the southern African country, Mediafax said.
A further 5,000 tonnes of maize from the western Tete province is likely to be sold to Malawi.
Exports are being handled by private company V & M which is currently negotiating with World Food Programme (WFP) to export a further 11,400 tonnes of Mozambican maize to WFP operations in Angola.
The company is also studying the possibility of exporting peanuts from northern Mozambique.
Mediafax said maize for export was purchased from peasant farmers for prices ranging from 650 to 800 meticais (5.5 to 8 U.S. cents) a kilo.

Mozambican farmers produced over 1.37 million tonnes of grain in this year's harvest, up 22 percent on the 1995 figure, Agriculture and Fisheries Minister Carlos Agostinho do Rosario said last week. Maize formed the bulk of the harvest with an estimated crop of about 947,000 tonnes, a rise of 29 percent on last year, said Rosario.
